message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a purchase: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), operating income of $123.2 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion — a business generating roughly $118 billion in annual operating cash while returning $95.0 billion via buybacks and $15.2 billion in dividends. Gross margin improved to 46.2% from 44.1%, driven by Services revenue up 13% to $96.2 billion at a 73.9% gross margin, which offsets flat iPhone sales ($201.2 billion) and an 8% decline in Greater China ($67.0 billion). Net income fell 3.4% year over year, but that was almost entirely a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge from the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not an operating deterioration; the balance sheet remains strong with $140.8 billion in unrestricted cash and marketable securities. I noted the risk factors (DOJ antitrust suit, DMA noncompliance exposure of up to 10% of worldwide net sales, supply-chain concentration) but judged them manageable against the cash generation. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed one buy limit order for 40 shares at $223.00 — a limit essentially at market — which filled at $223.00 for a total of $8,920, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, leaving the remaining cash in the account and moving no money out.
